relationships.subject: 2-AG
relationships.evidence_quote: 2-AG is subsequently released and acts as a retrograde messenger by activating presynaptic CB1Rs to mediate DSI

relationships.subject: CB1R
relationships.evidence_quote: which in turn activate presynaptic CB1Rs and inhibit GABA release, thereby inducing DSI

relationships.subject: DAGLα
relationships.evidence_quote: DAG is then converted into 2-AG by diacylglycerol lipase α (DAGLα) localized on the inner leaflet of the postsynaptic plasma membrane

relationships.subject: MAGL
relationships.evidence_quote: 2-AG signaling is terminated by hydrolysis into arachidonic acid and glycerol by the enzyme monoacylglycerol lipase (MAGL)

relationships.subject: FABP5
relationships.evidence_quote: FABP5 is released by primary astrocytes in vitro, localizes to synapses, and is indispensable for retrograde 2-AG signaling at glutamate synapses of the DRn

key_findings: Review of intracellular and synaptic endocannabinoid transport, including FABP5 carriers
Endocannabinoids act as retrograde messengers suppressing GABA and glutamate release via CB1R
